newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco raises customs duty on soft wheat imports.
newsitem.headline: Morocco raises customs duty on soft wheat imports.

text.p: The Moroccan cabinet on Wednesday approved a law raising customs duties on imported soft wheat to 59 percent from 35 percent, the official news agency MAP said.
It said the increase was "because of the importance of the national stock in this foodstuff and the relative fall in its price at the international level."
Further comment was not immediately available.
Morocco plans to import one million tonnes of soft wheat in the 1996/97 season (July-June), the agriculture ministry has said.
Heavy rains last month, which flooded some areas of the country, were not expected to have an impact on the imports, a ministry spokesman said on Tuesday.
In 1995, Morocco suffered a catastrophic drought and had to import some 2.4 million tonnes of cereals, including wheat.
